statement: Let ρ1, ρ2 be two regularized class laws, possibly equal, and write Mj, Aj,n, Ij and kj for their profiles and associated quantities from Section 6. Let X, Y be occupied cells of depth a. Put X1 = X, X2 = Y , and let b (j) z (w) be an admissible endpoint symbol on Xj in the sense of Definition 7.1. Let L be the largest nominal length of a descriptor in either symbol, with L = 0 if both lists are empty. Suppose that the integer depths satisfy 0 ≤ a < p ≤ v ≤ N and p − a ≤ v − p + 2σN, L ≤ v − p + 2σN, v − p ≥ 10σN. (8.1) At endpoint j, suppose that the symbol imposes the parallel test [gj, p] at a level ℓj ∈ {0, . . . , J0}: for ρj-almost every z ∈ Xj and every w ∈ Sd−1, b(j) z (w) ̸= 0 =⇒ w ∈ G (j) ℓj,[gj,p](z). (8.2) The superscript j indicates the class used in the test. Assume a ≤ gj < p, gj ≤ a + 2σN. (8.3) Form the general independent energy HX,Y (a, v) of Definition 7.3 using these specified symbols. For every fixed T > 0, HX,Y (a, v) ≤ R − ∑︁2 j=1 (Aj,p−Aj,a)+minj=1,2 kj(a,p)+Od(σ)+o(1) · max P⊂X, Q⊂Y P,Q occupied depth-p cells HP,Q (p, v) + O(R−T ). (8.4) No separation of X and Y is required. Every child in (8.4) is formed by restricting the same endpoint symbols to P and Q. It retains every original mask factor, including any whose anchor is p. Constants are uniform over cells and allowed symbols with fixed list-size exponents and derivative THE FALCONER DISTANCE CONJECTURE 43 budgets, and with fixed common numerical bounds for their smooth angular factors at the derivative orders used. The o(1) tends to zero as N → ∞ with these bounds, the parameters, and T fixed.
